model: General insurer free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; attributable earnings after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero, USD flows converted to the AUD quote at fx_rate)
model_label: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity, component-built on net insurance revenue (management basis): underwriting margin (100 - COR) + net insurance finance + investment income on policyholders' and shareholders' funds - financing costs - AT1 distributions - other, taxed at ~25%, less equity retained to hold the APRA PCA multiple as premium grows. Same family as IAG.AX (2026-09-23); BVPS x sustainable-P/B cross-check in inputs.notes.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 NET INSURANCE REVENUE on the management basis = insurance revenue 22,955 less management reinsurance expenses 4,543 (FY25 AR lines 832-833; divisions 4,773 + 8,882 + 4,757 = 18,412, lines 1005/1035/1083). NOT the CSV 'revenue' column (22,955 = AASB 17 gross insurance revenue) and NOT GWP (23,959): the combined operating ratio management guides (~92.5% FY26) is stated on net insurance revenue, so it is the base the margin path multiplies. Series: FY22 15,158, FY23 16,600, FY24 17,807, FY25 18,412; H1 FY26 9,545 (+8% headline, +4% constant currency).
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,494m ordinary shares on issue at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 FY26 report line 657; down from 1,506m at 31 Dec 2025 after the A$450m on-market buyback completed in H1 FY26) plus 12m weighted dilutive potential shares under the Employee Share and Option Plan (H1 FY26 line 1952). Held FLAT: SBC ($64m FY25, $38m H1 FY26) is expensed inside the flows and ESOP awards are satisfied by on-market purchase (line 748), so charging dilution as well would double-count. The 5m dilutive shares from the A$500m convertible AT1 capital notes (line 1958) are EXCLUDED: they are regulatory capital that converts at market price, and their distribution is charged in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO. The flow discounted is attributable profit AFTER financing costs ($248m FY25 on $3.7bn of Tier 2 subordinated notes, which are regulatory capital, not operating debt) and after the AT1 distribution. Deducting borrowings again would double-charge (SKILL.md: never subtract net debt from a post-interest flow). Cash of $2,325m sits inside the ~$36bn investment portfolio backing claims reserves and shareholders' funds, whose income is inside the flows, so it is not added either. total_debt and cash are audit-only.
inputs.total_debt_note: Borrowings 30 Jun 2026 (Metrics.csv), temporarily elevated by the EUR500m Tier 2 issue ahead of the A$500m Tier 2 redemption on 25 Aug 2026 and the US$524m 2046 notes redeemed Jun 2026; FY25 year-end 3,700, borrowings/total capital 24.1% (target 15-30%).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 free cash flow to equity: attributable NPAT 2,157 less ~577 equity retained for premium growth. Retention = 0.5 x ~1,155 of premium growth (midpoint of FY25 headline NIR growth of 605 -- depressed by higher Crop cessions, which carry little capital -- and GWP growth of 1,564), calibrated so that FY25 profit 'broadly offset capital consumed through ongoing premium growth and shareholder distributions' (AR line 1199): dividends A$1,642m ~ US$1,070m + A$450m buyback ~ US$300m + ~577 retained = ~1,950, with the PCA multiple drifting 1.86x -> 1.87x. Statutory OCF (4,223 FY25, 1,052 H1 FY26) and reported FCF are unusable: they swing with claims timing and investment-portfolio purchases.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory NPAT attributable to ordinary equity holders FY2025 (management basis identical; adjusted NPAT 2,132 after the $25m AT1 coupon, FY25 AR line 1216-1220). Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow (4,088) is OCF less capex and is not a distributable measure for an insurer.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment expense $64m FY25 / $59m FY24 (FY25 AR line 6228, statement of changes in equity; Metrics.csv StockBasedComp) is expensed inside the expense ratio and the flow starts from profit AFTER that charge, so no second deduction is made and sbc is recorded as 0 in the flows. House and street bases coincide (band collapsed).
inputs.interest_income_note: Investment income ($1,633m FY25 management basis = 1,036 policyholders' funds + 597 shareholders' funds, 4.9% return; $828m H1 FY26, 2.3%) is float income on ~$36bn of funds backing claims reserves and is CORE earnings for an insurer. It is LEFT IN the flows as its own component of the margin path, and the matching assets are not added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction). The Metrics.csv InterestIncome column (958 FY25) is 'interest received' from the cash flow statement, a subset.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: H1 FY26 purchase of treasury shares US$255m (A$450m programme completed in the half; FY25 $134m per AR line 8010, of which $60m in the Metrics.csv). The $900m May 2025 AT1 capital-notes buyback was a capital-structure swap into Tier 2 debt, not a share buyback.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate is AUD PER USD = 1 / AUDUSD 0.7016 = 1.4253 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-25 04:34 UTC, same hour as the price). The engine multiplies every USD per-share figure by it, so the canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are in AUD and comparable to current_price; the *_usd siblings hold the model-currency figures. No dual listing to parity-check (US OTC QBIEY is a thin ADR). FX is a real risk for AUD holders: QBE's AUD dividend and AUD value fall one-for-one with USD weakness, and the AUD has risen ~8% against the USD over 2026 (FY25 statutory EPS 141.3 USc = 219.1 Ac at the 2025 average rate of ~0.645).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the last completed fiscal year (Dec 2025); Y1 = FY2026, of which H1 is reported (NPAT 1,033, COR 92.8%, NIR 9,545). Year-1 drivers are the full-year FY26 guidance path reconciled to the H1 print.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (shares on issue) / H1 FY26 weighted dilutive ESOP shares
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the flows are USD (QBE reports in USD, ~74% of NIR is North America and International) and post-interest, with no debt deducted. US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sept 2026, assumed) + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta 1.05 (global commercial/specialty insurer with catastrophe, reserving and reinsurance-cycle exposure and a volatile FY17-FY20 record: NPAT -1,249 FY17, -1,517 FY20) = 9.45%, rounded to 9.5%. This is ~0.5pp above IAG's 9.0% AUD rate for the higher earnings beta of a cat-exposed global book. Catastrophe, reserving and pricing-cycle risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the rate (charge risk once). One rate across all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: lease principal and interest are inside the expense ratio and therefore inside the underwriting margin; lease liabilities ($230m FY25) are not debt in the model (which carries none).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial ($8m FY25, $8m FY24, <0.05% of NIR) and are folded into the -0.1% 'other' component of the margin path.
inputs.tax_note: 25% applied throughout: management's medium-term assumption is 'a Group tax rate of around 25%' (FY25 AR line 652); FY25 effective 23.9% (680/2,845), H1 FY26 24.9% (343/1,380) rising as International and Australia Pacific contribute more than lower-tax North America. Cash tax paid 399 FY25 / 341 FY24. No shelter, no ramp.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = net insurance revenue (management basis). ebitda_margin_path = management profit before tax / NIR = (100 - COR) underwriting margin + net insurance finance income/expense + fixed-income RFR adjustment + investment income on policyholders' and shareholders' funds - financing and other costs - AT1 distributions - other (gain on sale, associates, remediation, amortisation, NCI). FY25 actual: 8.1 (COR 91.9) - 0.3 (finance -53) + 0.3 (RFR +47) + 8.9 (1,633 investment) - 1.35 (248 financing) - 0.1 (18 - 5 - 20 - 14 = -21) = 15.45% -> 2,845 PBT, x0.761 = 2,165 less NCI 8 = 2,157 attributable. H1 FY26 actual: PBT 1,380 / 9,545 = 14.5%. da_pct_path = 0 (depreciation and intangible amortisation sit inside the expense ratio). sbc_pct_path = 0 (expensed in the expense ratio). capex_pct_path = equity retained to hold the APRA PCA multiple inside the 1.6-1.8x target as premium grows = 0.5 x NIR growth: shareholders' equity is 63% of NIR (11,667 / 18,412 H1 FY26), borrowings are 24% of total capital, and QBE reports that FY25 profit 'broadly offset' capital consumed by premium growth plus distributions with the PCA multiple flat (1.86x -> 1.87x) -- the PCA dollar amount itself is only disclosed in the investor pack, not the annual report. At 6% growth that is 3.0% of NIR (~$585m, ~28% of NPAT, consistent with the 50% dividend payout plus an ongoing buyback); at 2.5% terminal growth 1.25% of NIR (~11% of NPAT). FCF out of the engine is therefore FCFE = attributable NPAT - growth capital; it is what is available for dividends and buybacks.
inputs.notes: MODEL: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes an insurer to 'BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. QBE distributes 40-60% of adjusted NPAT as dividends plus buybacks (A$450m FY26) and its value is the distributable earnings stream on a premium base, so -- exactly as for IAG.AX (2026-09-23) -- the model discounts free cash flow to equity at the cost of equity with net debt at zero, built on the engine so the dashboard reproduces it. Memory has no QBE entry (first valuation). An owner-FCF DCF is impossible here: 'capex' in the cash flow statement is inseparable from investment-portfolio purchases and OCF (4,223 FY25 vs 1,503 FY23) is claims-timing noise. BVPS x SUSTAINABLE-P/B CROSS-CHECK (memo): BVPS 11,667 / 1,506 = US$7.75 = A$11.04; sustainable P/B at the medium-term 15% ROE guide = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = (0.15 - 0.025)/(0.095 - 0.025) = 1.79x -> A$19.7; at FY25's 19.8% adjusted ROE it would be 2.47x -> A$27.3. current_price is ~2.08x book and ~11.8x base FY26 EPS (~US$1.37 = A$1.95). The base case (~A$20-21) is the 15% ROE answer from the other side; the market is pricing something between the guide and the FY25 peak. NORMALISATION: FY25 (COR 91.9%, ROE 19.8%, catastrophe costs $751m vs $1,160m allowance, favourable PYD $449m, investment return 4.9%) is a decade high and management's own medium-term guide is 15%+ ROE 'assuming investment returns of 3%+', i.e. below FY25; renewal rate increases have collapsed from 5.5% (FY24) to 1.0% (FY25) to 0.3% (H1 FY26). The base therefore takes FY26 at guidance (COR ~92.5%) and fades the COR to 93.0% (the FY24/H1 FY26 level) and the investment return to 3.5% (above the 3% guide floor; core fixed income exit yield 4.1% at Jun-26). ANCHORS: FY25 NIR 18,412, GWP 23,959, statutory NPAT 2,157, adjusted NPAT 2,132, PBT 2,845, investment income 1,633 (4.9%), financing costs 248, PCA multiple 1.87x (1.73x pro forma dividend + buyback), DPS A$1.09 (50% payout). H1 FY26: NPAT 1,033, COR 92.8%, NIR 9,545, GWP 15,137 (+10% headline, +6% cc), investment income 828 (2.3% half-year), PCA 1.82x (1.78x pro forma interim dividend, -4pts for the Aug-26 A$500m Tier 2 redemption, +2pts for the H2 loss portfolio transfer), interim DPS A$0.33 (33% payout). FY26 guidance (reaffirmed 14 Aug 2026): COR ~92.5%, mid-single-digit constant-currency GWP growth, catastrophe allowance $1,130m, expense ratio ~12%. Metrics.csv 'Revenue' is AASB 17 insurance revenue (22,955) and FY21/FY22 are different revenue definitions (gross earned premium vs insurance revenue), so revenue CAGRs across FY22 are not one series; total assets drop ~51bn -> 39bn at FY22 is AASB 17 presentation, not real.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY26 guidance (mid-single-digit constant-currency GWP growth; H1 FY26 NIR +4% cc, +8% headline on AUD/GBP strength) less the NIR lag from higher Crop cessions; near-term NIR path, not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6.6-9.6%) sits well inside the revenue/GWP CAGRs, but the EPS and FCF (NPAT) 3-year CAGRs of 54-57% run from the FY22 trough (NPAT 587, COVID-era reserve strengthening and a 95.9% COR) to the FY25 decade-high and describe a turnaround, not a trend; the 5-year EPS/FCF CAGRs are undefined because FY20 was a loss (-1,517). Revenue 5-year CAGR mixes pre-AASB 17 gross earned premium (FY20 14,008) with AASB 17 insurance revenue (FY25 22,955). The clean series are NIR (FY22 15,158 -> FY25 18,412, 6.7%) and GWP (6.2% 3-year), both partly rate-driven in a hard market that has now ended; the projection fades them to 2.5%.
historical_growth.notes: revenue_* on Metrics.csv revenue (FY22 18,904 -> FY25 22,955; FY20 14,008 -> FY25 22,955, definition break at FY22). nir_3yr on management net insurance revenue. gwp_* on GWP (FY22 19,993 / FY20 14,643 -> FY25 23,959). eps_3yr on statutory EPS US$0.36 -> 1.40. equity_* on shareholders' equity (FY22 8,855 / FY20 8,491 -> FY25 11,671; FY24 includes 886 of AT1 notes classified as equity, bought back May 2025). fcf_3yr on attributable NPAT (587 -> 2,157), the numerator of the FCFE flow. dps_4yr on AUD DPS 30c FY21 -> 109c FY25. Ten-year management COR: FY16 ~94, FY17 ~104 (reserve strengthening), FY18 95.7, FY19 97.5, FY20 104.1 (COVID), FY21 93.7, FY22 95.9, FY23 95.2, FY24 93.1, FY25 91.9, H1 FY26 92.8 -- mean ~96.5 including the two blow-up years, ~94.5 excluding them; the FY23-25 improvement follows the exit of North America non-core lines, which the base treats as structural but only to 93.0%, not 91.9%.

base.growth_rationale: Net insurance revenue in USD. FY26 6.0%: H1 FY26 was +8% headline / +4% constant currency (GWP +10% / +6%), and the AUD and GBP have strengthened against the reporting USD; FY26 guidance is mid-single-digit constant-currency GWP growth with NIR lagging on Crop cessions. Then fades from mid-single-digit (renewal rate increases have fallen to 0.3%, so growth is now targeted volume in QBE Re, Cyber, Portfolio Solutions and North American specialty, plus low-to-mid single digit claims-inflation pass-through) to 2.5% terminal by FY34.
base.margin_rationale: Management pre-tax margin on NIR = underwriting margin + insurance finance + investment income - financing - AT1 - other. FY26: COR 92.5% (guidance; H1 92.8%) -> 7.5 underwriting - 0.3 insurance finance + 8.5 investment income (H1 FY26 828 on 9,545 = 8.7%, 4.6% annualised return on ~1.85x NIR of funds) - 1.4 financing (~$275m on the enlarged Tier 2 stack) - 0.1 AT1 (A$500m notes issued Aug-26, part year) - 0.1 other = 14.1% (H1 FY26 actual 14.5%; H2 carries the Atlantic hurricane and Australian storm seasons). FY27: COR 93.0% (the FY24 / H1 FY26 level; rate increases ~0%, claims inflation low-to-mid single digit, Accident & Health and large-loss pressure persisting), investment return 4.3% -> 8.0%, financing -1.35, AT1 -0.15: 7.0 - 0.3 + 8.0 - 1.35 - 0.15 - 0.1 = 13.1 -> 13.2 with a modest catastrophe-allowance beat. FY28 7.0 - 0.3 + 7.4 (4.0%) - 1.3 - 0.15 - 0.1 = 12.6. FY29 investment 7.0 (3.75%) -> 12.2. FY30+ COR 93.0%, investment return 3.5% (6.5% of NIR; above management's 3%+ floor, below the 4.1% Jun-26 core fixed-income exit yield), financing 1.2, AT1 0.15, other 0.1 = 11.8%. Long-run NPAT ~US$2.0bn on ~US$13.5bn of equity = ~15% ROE, i.e. the medium-term guide. FY26 NPAT ~US$2,060m (EPS ~US$1.37 / A$1.95), FY27 ~2,030.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold the PCA multiple inside 1.6-1.8x as premium grows: 0.5 x NIR growth (see engine_mapping). FY26 3.0% of NIR (~$585m, ~28% of NPAT; the balance is the 40-60% dividend plus buybacks), fading to 1.25% at 2.5% terminal growth (~11% of NPAT retained). The H2 FY26 loss portfolio transfer (+2pts PCA) roughly offsets the Aug-26 Tier 2 redemption (-4pts) and the interim dividend, so no one-off capital release is bridged.

bull.growth_rationale: FY26 at the top of guidance with FX tailwind (+7% USD NIR), then the growth franchises (QBE Re, Cyber, Portfolio Solutions, North American Construction/Healthcare/Specialty Casualty) compound at 5-6% for four years as the portfolio-exit drag is gone and capital-efficient structures (cat bond, casualty sidecar) let QBE write more on the same capital; fades to 3.0% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: COR beats guidance again at 92.0% in FY26 (as FY25 beat 92.5% with 91.9%) and holds at 92.0% as the North America turnaround (97.3% COR) closes toward International (91.6%), the expense ratio falls below 12% on the Guidewire/AI programme, and reserving initiatives keep producing favourable PYD; investment return stays at 4.5% (8.5% -> 8.0% of NIR as the ratio of funds to NIR drifts down). FY26: 8.0 - 0.3 + 8.5 - 1.4 - 0.1 - 0.1 = 14.6. Long run: 8.0 - 0.3 + 7.5 - 1.2 - 0.15 - 0.1 = 13.75 -> 13.5 with a little cat normalisation. Sustained ROE ~17-18%, between the guide and FY25.
bull.capex_rationale: Same 0.5 x growth retention rule on the faster path; sidecar and cat-bond capital is assumed to keep the intensity at 0.5 rather than lower it, which is conservative for the bull.

bear.growth_rationale: FY26 lands at the bottom of guidance in constant currency and the AUD/GBP tailwind reverses in H2 (+4% USD NIR); then the soft market bites -- property and Lloyd's rates go negative, LMI keeps shrinking with Australian mortgage origination, Crop cessions rise -- and QBE holds discipline by shedding volume, so NIR grows ~2% a year, below claims inflation.
bear.margin_rationale: FY26 COR 94.0% (a heavy H2 catastrophe season takes cat costs to allowance and Accident & Health / large losses continue): 6.0 - 0.3 + 8.0 - 1.45 - 0.1 - 0.1 = 12.1. FY27 COR 95.0% -- the FY22/FY23 level -- as soft pricing meets claims inflation and a reserve-strengthening year in International Liability/Marine; investment return falls toward management's 3% floor as rates are cut (7.0% of NIR): 5.0 - 0.3 + 7.0 - 1.5 - 0.15 - 0.1 = 10.0 -> 10.1. FY28 onward COR 94.5% (roughly the ten-year mean excluding the two blow-up years) with investment income at 3.0-3.2% of funds (6.3% -> 5.5% of NIR), financing 1.5% on a flat premium base: 5.5 - 0.3 + 5.5 - 1.5 - 0.15 - 0.1 = 9.0 -> 9.1. ROE ~11-12%: no solvency question (PCA 1.8x, AA- rating, quota shares and cat bond), so the bear is an earnings-and-multiple case, not a survival case -- FY17/FY20-style losses are not modelled because the exited lines that produced them are gone.
bear.capex_rationale: Higher capital intensity (0.55 x growth): APRA insurance-risk charges rise with catastrophe allowances and the LPT/sidecar relief is not repeated, so a larger share of a smaller profit is retained; buybacks stop.

scenario_narratives.base: QBE delivers FY26 on guidance (COR ~92.5%, NIR +6% in USD with the FX tailwind, NPAT ~US$2.06bn) and then normalises toward its own medium-term guide: the COR drifts to 93.0% as renewal rate increases sit near zero and claims inflation runs low-to-mid single digit, the investment return eases from 4.9% to 3.5% as rates fall, and premium growth fades from mid-single-digit to 2.5%. Around 70-90% of profit is distributed (40-60% dividend plus buybacks); the rest funds the regulatory capital a growing premium base requires. Long-run ROE settles at ~15%, which is what management guides. The axes that matter are the catastrophe allowance versus experience, prior-year development, North America's 97% COR, and yields on ~US$36bn of funds.
scenario_narratives.bull: The underwriting turnaround is structural: COR holds at 92.0% (North America closes toward International, expense ratio below 12%, reserving initiatives keep releasing), investment returns stay at 4.5% in a higher-for-longer rate world, and the growth franchises compound NIR at 5-6% for four years on capital-efficient structures. ROE sustains at 17-18% -- between the 15% guide and FY25's 19.8% -- and value is capped at a 16x terminal multiple on free cash to equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pricing cycle turns: property and Lloyd's rates go negative, a heavy H2 FY26 catastrophe season takes cat costs to allowance, FY27 brings a 95% COR with reserve strengthening in International long-tail lines, and rate cuts pull the investment return to management's 3% floor. QBE sheds volume to hold discipline, so NIR grows ~2% and ROE settles at 11-12%. No solvency question (PCA 1.8x, AA-), so this is an earnings-and-multiple case: FY17/FY20-style losses are not modelled because the lines that produced them have been exited.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: catastrophe/climate exposure is rated high in the Analysis JSON, FY25 was flattered by cat costs $400m+ below allowance and $449m of favourable PYD, and renewal rate increases have collapsed to 0.3% -- the soft-market bear is the live cycle risk. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires the decade-high FY25 settings (92% COR, 4.5%+ investment return) to persist through a softening market, which management's own 15%+ ROE guide (below FY25's 19.8%) does not assume. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: QBE is valued on the cash it can actually pay its shareholders: attributable profit after the interest on its Tier 2 capital and the AT1 distribution, less the equity it must retain to keep the APRA PCA multiple at target as premium grows, discounted at a 9.5% USD cost of equity with no separate debt deduction and converted to AUD at spot. The base case takes FY26 at guidance and then normalises the COR to 93% and the investment return to 3.5% -- roughly management's 15%+ medium-term ROE guide -- which lands modestly below the current price; the market is capitalising something between that guide and the FY25 decade-high (91.9% COR, 19.8% ROE). A BVPS x sustainable-P/B cross-check (15% ROE, 9.5% CoE, 2.5% g -> 1.79x book -> ~A$19.7) gives the same answer from the balance-sheet side. AUD holders also carry the USD translation risk: every 5% move in AUD/USD moves the AUD value ~5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Catastrophe experience versus the $1,130m allowance is the single largest swing: each $100m of pre-tax overrun is ~0.5pp of COR and ~US$0.05 of EPS; climate is raising the allowance every year.
Prior-year development has been a consistent tailwind (+$449m FY25, +$403m H1 FY26); a return to the adverse development of FY17-FY20 is the bear case's second leg and is not in the base.
The soft market: renewal rate increases have gone 5.5% -> 1.0% -> 0.3% in eighteen months; the base assumes the COR gives back only ~1pt to 93.0%, the bear 3pts.
Investment return: ~US$36bn of funds at a 4.9% FY25 return; the base fades to 3.5% (each 50bp is ~US$180m pre-tax, ~1pt of NIR margin) and management's own floor is 3%.
Currency: financials are USD, the quote and dividend are AUD; the AUD has risen ~8% against the USD in 2026 and the AUD value here scales with the fx_rate.

Capital retention is modelled at 0.5 x NIR growth on a PCA that the annual report does not disclose in dollars; an APRA change or a shift toward long-tail / reinsurance business raises the intensity and cuts FCFE.
Discount rate: the base is terminal-heavy and the 14x FCFE cap binds; each 1pp on the cost of equity moves the value ~12-15%.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API, QBE.AX regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of (regular session); 52-week range 18.57-25.83. FX: Yahoo AUDUSD=X at the same hour, see inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: QBE.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (H1 FY2016-H1 FY2026, USD millions); QBE.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt summary financial performance (lines 829-869), underwriting performance (892-965), statutory-to-management reconciliation (1310-1346), capital and adjusted NPAT (1193-1242), EPS note 5.5 (11797-11815); QBE.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt summary (375-399), divisional NIR (521/547/590), capital (684-692), adjusted NPAT (701-729), outlook (753-759), EPS denominator (1949-1958); QBE.AX_Annual_FY2023.txt management reinsurance expenses (1285/1324) for the NIR series
data_sources.qualitative: QBE.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-25); FY25 Annual Report 2026 outlook (COR ~92.5%, mid-single-digit cc GWP growth, catastrophe allowance $1,130m, expense ratio ~12%, medium-term 15%+ adjusted ROE at 3%+ investment returns and ~25% tax), reaffirmed in the H1 FY26 report of 14 Aug 2026
